findings.claim: Non-ASCII source paths now resolve; ls-files -z is split on NUL.
has_passed is now now >= stale_after, per OKF 5.5.
A source naming a tracked folder now resolves and is dated by git log.
test_exit_and_json now asserts the fixture is due and checks the --json exit code.

The review due help text still says a source that resolves to no tracked file becomes a notice. Since f3, a tracked folder also resolves, so the help should say 'no tracked file or folder'. Agents read this help to know which source forms work.

verdict.text: All four round-1 findings are fixed, and each fix has a test that fails without it.

The `>=` change in the shared `has_passed` keeps review-due and handoffs consistent: a handoff at its exact stale_after instant is now expired in both, and the handoffs docstring ("has not passed") still reads true.
One non-blocking docs finding is left: the help text does not mention folders.
Ran `loopctl gate stamp` in the worktree: lint, format, tests and eval rows r1 to r7 all pass, "stamp green: 58eb8bdae514...".
Read the round's changes in src/kmctl/review_due.py, src/kmctl/okf.py, tests/test_review_due.py and tests/test_handoffs.py, and how handoffs.py uses has_passed.
In a scratch copy, I reverted the `-z` split and the folder check one at a time, with PYTHONPATH pointing at the copy.
test_due_source_with_non_ascii_name and test_due_source_folder then both fail, so they test the fixes.
core.quotePath is not set globally, so the café test runs with git's default quoting.
test_has_passed_at_the_exact_instant asserts True at the same instant and False one second earlier, which fails under the old `<`.
r7 now asserts `data["due"] == ["new"]` and both exit codes are 0.
The `_git` strip() leaves NUL separators intact.
The folder check skips the repository root (empty rel), so `.` still gives a notice.
f1 resolved: `ls-files -z` split on NUL at review_due.py:158-159, covered by test_due_source_with_non_ascii_name.
f2 resolved: okf.py has_passed uses `now >= when`, and its docstring cites §5.5.
f3 resolved: `_resolve` accepts a path with a tracked file under it, covered by test_due_source_folder.
f4 resolved: test_exit_and_json asserts the due list and the --json exit code.
f5 (non-blocking): a one-line help text change.
A plain fix is enough, so it does not need to come back to me.
